259: /****************************************************************************
260:  * Name: netdev_upper_txpoll
261:  *
262:  * Description:
263:  *   The transmitter is available, check if the network has any outgoing
264:  *   packets ready to send.  This is a callback from devif_poll().
265:  *   devif_poll() may be called:
266:  *
267:  *   1. When the preceding TX packet send is complete
268:  *   2. When the preceding TX packet send times out and the interface is
269:  *      reset
270:  *   3. During normal TX polling
271:  *
272:  * Input Parameters:
273:  *   dev - Reference to the NuttX driver state structure
274:  *
275:  * Returned Value:
276:  *   Negated errno value - Error number that occurs.
277:  *   NETDEV_TX_CONTINUE  - Driver can send more, continue the poll.
278:  *
279:  * Assumptions:
280:  *   Called with the network locked.
281:  *
282:  ****************************************************************************/
283: 
284: static int netdev_upper_txpoll(FAR struct net_driver_s *dev)
285: {
286:   FAR struct netdev_upperhalf_s *upper = dev->d_private;
287:   FAR struct netdev_lowerhalf_s *lower = upper->lower;
288:   FAR netpkt_t                  *pkt;
289:   int                            ret;
290: 
291:   DEBUGASSERT(dev->d_len > 0);
292: 
293:   NETDEV_TXPACKETS(dev);
294: 
295: #ifdef CONFIG_NET_PKT
296:   /* When packet sockets are enabled, loopback the tx frame to pkt socket
297:    * who has protocl type of ETH_P_ALL
298:    */
299: 
300:   pkt_loopback(dev);
301: #endif
302: 
303:   pkt = netpkt_get(dev, NETPKT_TX);
304: 
305:   if (netpkt_getdatalen(lower, pkt) > NETDEV_PKTSIZE(dev))
306:     {
307:       nerr("ERROR: Packet too long to send!\n");
308:       ret = -EMSGSIZE;
309:     }
310:   else
311:     {
312:       ret = lower->ops->transmit(lower, pkt);
313:     }
314: 
315:   if (ret != OK)
316:     {
317:       /* Stop polling on any error
318:        * REVISIT: maybe store the pkt in upper half and retry later?
319:        */
320: 
321:       NETDEV_TXERRORS(dev);
322:       nerr("ERROR: Transmit failed: %d\n", ret);
323:       netpkt_put(dev, pkt, NETPKT_TX);
324:       return ret;
325:     }
326: 
327:   return NETDEV_TX_CONTINUE;
328: }

803:  *   The loop for dedicated thread.
804:  *
805:  ****************************************************************************/

807: static int netdev_upper_loop(int argc, FAR char *argv[])
808: {
809:   FAR struct netdev_upperhalf_s *upper =
810:     (FAR struct netdev_upperhalf_s *)((uintptr_t)strtoul(argv[1], NULL, 16));
811:   int cpu = atoi(argv[2]);
812:   FAR struct netdev_thread_s *t = &upper->thread[cpu];

814:   if (upper->lower->rxtype == NETDEV_RX_THREAD_RSS)
815:     {
816:       cpu_set_t cpuset;
817: 
818:       CPU_ZERO(&cpuset);
819:       CPU_SET(cpu, &cpuset);
820:       sched_setaffinity(t->tid, sizeof(cpu_set_t), &cpuset);
821:     }
822: 
823:   while (nxsem_wait(&t->sem) == OK && t->tid != INVALID_PROCESS_ID)
824:     {
825:       netdev_upper_work(upper);
826:     }
827: 
828:   nwarn("WARNING: Netdev work thread quitting.");
829:   nxsem_post(&t->sem_exit);
830:   return 0;

836:  * Description:
837:  *   Called when there is any work to do.
838:  *
839:  * Input Parameters:
840:  *   dev - Reference to the NuttX driver state structure
841:  *
842:  ****************************************************************************/
843: 
844: static inline void netdev_upper_queue_work(FAR struct net_driver_s *dev)
845: {
846:   FAR struct netdev_upperhalf_s *upper = dev->d_private;
847:   int cpu = 0;
848: 
849:   switch (upper->lower->rxtype)
850:     {
851:       case NETDEV_RX_WORK:
852:         {
853:           FAR struct work_s *work = upper->work;
854:           if (work_available(work))
855:             {
856:               /* Schedule to serialize the poll on the worker thread. */
857: 
858:               work_queue(upper->lower->priority, work, netdev_upper_work,
859:                          upper, 0);
860:             }
861:         }
862:         break;
863:       case NETDEV_RX_THREAD_RSS:
864:         cpu = this_cpu();
865:       case NETDEV_RX_THREAD:
866:         {
867:           FAR struct netdev_thread_s *t = &upper->thread[cpu];
868:           int semcount;
869: 
870:           if (nxsem_get_value(&t->sem, &semcount) == OK && semcount <= 0)
871:             {
872:               nxsem_post(&t->sem);
873:             }
874:         }
875:         break;
876:     }

198: static int ipv4_in(FAR struct net_driver_s *dev)

296: 
297: #endif

482: #endif

486: #endif

488: #ifdef CONFIG_NET_IPFILTER

494: #endif

497: 
498:   switch (ipv4->proto)

500: #ifdef NET_TCP_HAVE_STACK
501:       case IP_PROTO_TCP:   /* TCP input */
502:         tcp_ipv4_input(dev);
503:         break;
504: #endif
505: 
506: #ifdef NET_UDP_HAVE_STACK

510: #endif

512: #ifdef NET_ICMP_HAVE_STACK

515:       case IP_PROTO_ICMP:  /* ICMP input */

518: #endif
519: 
520: #ifdef CONFIG_NET_IGMP
521:   /* Check for IGMP input */
522: 
523:       case IP_PROTO_IGMP:  /* IGMP input */
524:         igmp_input(dev);

526: #endif

529: #ifdef CONFIG_NET_STATISTICS

531:         g_netstats.ipv4.protoerr++;

681:  *   domain - IP domain (PF_INET or PF_INET6)

692: static void tcp_input(FAR struct net_driver_s *dev, uint8_t domain,
693:                       unsigned int iplen)
694: {
695:   FAR struct tcp_conn_s *conn = NULL;

699:   uint32_t flags;
700:   uint16_t tmp16;

704: #ifdef CONFIG_NET_STATISTICS

707:   g_netstats.tcp.recv++;

710:   /* Get a pointer to the TCP header.  The TCP header lies just after the

714:   tcp = IPBUF(iplen);

716:   /* Get the size of the IP header and the TCP header.
717:    *
718:    * REVISIT:  TCP header is *not* a constant!  It can be larger if the
719:    * TCP header includes options.  The constant TCP_HDRLEN should be
720:    * replaced with the macro TCP_OPT_HDRLEN(n) which will calculate the

726: #ifdef CONFIG_NET_TCP_CHECKSUMS

729:   if (((dev->d_features & NETDEV_RX_CSUM) == 0)

732:       /* Compute and check the TCP checksum. */

734: #ifdef CONFIG_NET_STATISTICS

740:     }
741: #endif

101: /* This structure is the generic form of state structure used by lower half
102:  * netdev driver. This state structure is passed to the netdev driver when
103:  * the driver is initialized. Then, on subsequent callbacks into the lower
104:  * half netdev logic, this structure is provided so that the netdev logic can
105:  * maintain state information.
106:  *
107:  * Normally that netdev logic will have its own, custom state structure
108:  * that is simply cast to struct netdev_lowerhalf_s. In order to perform such
109:  * casts, the initial fields of the custom state structure match the initial

309: static void *vp_thread(void *arg)
310: {
311:   (void)arg;
312: 
313:   for (; ; )
314:     {
315:       struct pollfd pfd;
316:       uint32_t generation = 0;
317:       int save_status = 0;
318:       bool saved = false;
319:       bool stopping;
320:       int fd;
321:       int ret;
322: 
323:       pthread_mutex_lock(&g_lock);
324:       stopping = g_server.stopping;
325:       pthread_mutex_unlock(&g_lock);
326:       if (stopping)
327:         {
328:           break;
329:         }
330: 
331:       pfd.fd = g_server.listenfd;
332:       pfd.events = POLLIN;
333:       pfd.revents = 0;
334: 
335:       /* Polling rather than blocking in accept(): stop() then needs no signal
336:        * and no socket shutdown trick that may or may not wake accept on a
337:        * given stack.
338:        *
339:        * This requires CONFIG_NET_TCPBACKLOG on NuttX, which the Kconfig
340:        * depends on.  Without it TCP_BACKLOG events never fire, POLLIN on a
341:        * listening socket is unreachable, and accept() blocks with no timeout
342:        * at all -- measured on the board as a service that reported
343:        * "listening" and then answered nothing.
344:        */
345: 
346:       ret = poll(&pfd, 1, VP_ACCEPT_POLL_MS);
347:       if (ret < 0)
348:         {
349:           if (errno == EINTR)
350:             {
351:               continue;
352:             }
353: 
354:           break;
355:         }
356: 
357:       if (ret == 0)
358:         {
359:           continue;
360:         }
361: 
362:       fd = accept(g_server.listenfd, NULL, NULL);
363:       if (fd < 0)
364:         {
365:           if (errno == EINTR || errno == ECONNABORTED)
366:             {
367:               continue;
368:             }
369: 
370:           break;
371:         }
372: 
373:       vp_handle(fd, &saved, &save_status, &generation);
374: 
375:       /* Close before notifying.  The application is expected to leave SoftAP
376:        * from the callback, and doing that with the response still in flight is
377:        * what makes a successful save look like a failed submit on the phone.
378:        */
379: 
380:       shutdown(fd, SHUT_RDWR);
381:       close(fd);
382: 
383:       if (saved)
384:         {
385:           pthread_mutex_lock(&g_lock);
386:           g_server.generation = generation;
387:           pthread_mutex_unlock(&g_lock);
388:         }
389: 
390:       if (saved || save_status < 0)
391:         {
392:           if (g_server.on_saved != NULL)
393:             {
394:               g_server.on_saved(save_status, generation, g_server.cb_arg);
395:             }
396:         }
397: 
398:       if (saved && g_server.one_shot)
399:         {
400:           break;
401:         }
402: 
403:       pthread_mutex_lock(&g_lock);
404:       stopping = g_server.stopping;
405:       pthread_mutex_unlock(&g_lock);
406:       if (stopping)
407:         {
408:           break;
409:         }
410:     }
411: 
412:   pthread_mutex_lock(&g_lock);
413:   if (g_server.listenfd >= 0)
414:     {
415:       close(g_server.listenfd);
416:       g_server.listenfd = -1;
417:     }
418: 
419:   g_server.state = VP_STATE_FINISHED;
420:   pthread_mutex_unlock(&g_lock);
421:   return NULL;
422: }

## Verdict

`NET_LL_IEEE80211` is correct **for this BK7258 lower-half as implemented**, provided the firmware/CP supplies and accepts Ethernet-II/802.3 data frames—not raw 802.11 MAC frames.

Changing the registration to `NET_LL_ETHERNET` is **not the minimal fix**. In this NuttX tree, both link types use the same 14-byte Ethernet header handling and the same `eth_input()` path. The distinction is mainly that `IEEE80211` gives the interface a WLAN name/identity and wireless ioctl behavior.

The concrete source-confirmed configuration issue is `CONFIG_NET_TCPBACKLOG`:

- The `nsh` configuration has TCP enabled but does **not** enable TCP backlog.
- The provisioning HTTP server source explicitly documents that without TCP backlog, the listener can report “listening” but never become poll-readable, resulting in no useful HTTP connection.
- The `ai_agent` configuration already enables TCP backlog, so that build needs runtime packet/log discrimination rather than a link-type change.

```c
ret = netdev_lower_register(&g_wifi.lower, NET_LL_IEEE80211);
```

### What NuttX does with that type

`nuttx/include/nuttx/net/net.h`

- Lines **118–130** define the link types.
- `NET_LL_ETHERNET` and `NET_LL_IEEE80211` are separate enum values, but neither indicates that the packet buffer contains raw 802.11 management/data headers.

`nuttx/net/netdev/netdev_register.c`

- Lines **317–324**: `NET_LL_ETHERNET` uses:
  - `llhdrlen = ETH_HDRLEN`
  - Ethernet packet size
  - broadcast/multicast flags
- Lines **326–333**: `NET_LL_IEEE80211` uses exactly the same:
  - `llhdrlen = ETH_HDRLEN`
  - Ethernet packet size
  - broadcast/multicast flags

Therefore, in this tree, `NET_LL_IEEE80211` still means a 14-byte Ethernet-compatible L2 header for the IP stack.

The resulting fields are defined in `nuttx/include/nuttx/net/netdev.h`:

- `d_lltype`: lines **343–348**
- `d_llhdrlen`: line **348**
- `d_pktsize`: lines **353–354**

### BK7258 RX copies the complete Ethernet frame

`bk7258_wifi.c`

- Lines **1297–1337**, `wifi_copy_rx_frame()`:
  - validates the CPDU/pbuf
  - requires a nonzero packet length
  - limits the frame to `BK7258_WIFI_MAX_FRAME`
  - copies the CP pbuf payload verbatim into `packet->frame`
  - records the full length in `packet->length`

Relevant checks are lines **1319–1324**:

```c
pbuf.len > BK7258_WIFI_MAX_FRAME
pbuf.tot_len != pbuf.len
!wifi_cp_pointer(pbuf.payload, pbuf.len)
```

The driver’s own AP RX trace also interprets bytes 12–13 as an Ethernet EtherType:

- Lines **1577–1583**:

```c
uint16_t type = ((uint16_t)frame[12] << 8) | frame[13];
printf("... len=%u eth=0x%04x\n", ...);
```

That is direct evidence that the driver expects a complete Ethernet-II frame.

### BK7258 TX also sends the complete Ethernet frame

`bk7258_wifi.c`

- Lines **1918–1937**, `wifi_transmit()`:
  - obtains the complete netpkt length
  - rejects zero/oversize frames
  - requires carrier, active role, and mailbox readiness
- Lines **1958–1971**:
  - sets the CP pbuf length to the entire netpkt length
  - copies the complete netpkt into `tx->frame`
- Lines **1978–1985** trace bytes 12–13 as Ethernet EtherType.
- Lines **1994–2005** submits that frame to the BK7258 CP.

There is no L2 conversion from Ethernet to raw 802.11 in this lower half. That is appropriate if the BK controller’s data channel expects Ethernet MSDUs and performs WiFi encapsulation internally.

**Conclusion:** `NET_LL_IEEE80211` plus full Ethernet frames is internally consistent and is not the cause of a TCP-only failure.

## 2. RX path: lower half → `eth_input()` → IPv4/TCP

### CP RX notification

`bk7258_wifi.c`

- Lines **1648–1697**, `wifi_mailbox_rx()`:
  - validates a CP data node
  - queues it for the worker
  - reserves recycle state
- Lines **1709–1775**, `wifi_worker()`:
  - processes data nodes with `wifi_handle_data()`
  - calls `wifi_notify_network()`

`wifi_handle_data()`:

- Lines **1450–1645**
- Validates every CPDU/pbuf in the list.
- Copies valid RX frames into the driver RX queue at lines **1566–1587**.
- Sets `notifications->rxready = true` at lines **1631–1634**.

`wifi_notify_network()`:

- Lines **1258–1270**
- Calls:

```c
netdev_lower_rxready(&g_wifi.lower);
```

### Lower-half work scheduling

`nuttx/drivers/net/netdev_upperhalf.c`

- Lines **1665–1678**, `netdev_lower_rxready()`:
  - because BK7258 uses `NETDEV_RX_WORK`, queues upper-half network work.
- Lines **785–797**, `netdev_upper_work()`:
  - processes RX first
  - then processes TX availability
- Lines **708–772**, `netdev_upper_rxpoll_work()`:
  - repeatedly calls the lower-half `receive()` callback
  - drops packets if the interface is down
  - places the packet into the network device buffer
  - selects the protocol path based on `d_lltype`

The key switch is lines **738–752**:

```c
case NET_LL_ETHERNET:
case NET_LL_IEEE80211:
    eth_input(dev);
    break;
```

Thus `NET_LL_IEEE80211` is explicitly routed to `eth_input()`.

### Ethernet demultiplexing

`nuttx/drivers/net/netdev_upperhalf.c`

`eth_input()` is lines **519–625**.

- Line **521** treats `NETLLBUF` as `struct eth_hdr_s`.
- Lines **567–578**:
  - Ethernet type `0x0800` → `ipv4_input(dev)`
- Lines **593–602**:
  - Ethernet type `0x0806` → `arp_input(dev)`
- Lines **605–610**:
  - all other EtherTypes are dropped
- Lines **617–624**:
  - if protocol processing creates a response, queue it for TX

This explains why ARP and IPv4/DHCP can work with the current link type: both use this same Ethernet-II demultiplexer.

### IPv4 processing

`nuttx/net/devif/ipv4_input.c`

- Lines **198–219**, `ipv4_in()`:
  - calls `arp_ipin(dev)`
- Lines **235–247**:
  - validates IPv4 version/header length
- Lines **249–285**:
  - subtracts `NET_LL_HDRLEN(dev)` from `d_len`
  - checks the IP total length
- Lines **394–461**:
  - verifies that the destination IP belongs to the device
- Lines **473–485**:
  - validates the IPv4 checksum when RX checksum offload is not enabled
- Lines **496–509**:
  - dispatches by IP protocol:
    - TCP → `tcp_ipv4_input(dev)`
    - UDP → `udp_ipv4_input(dev)`
- Lines **557–560**:
  - invokes `devif_out(dev)` after protocol processing.

The public wrapper at lines **596–623** restores the original buffer pointer after processing.

For a TCP SYN, the required path is therefore:

```text
eth_input()
  → ipv4_input()
    → ipv4_in()
      → tcp_ipv4_input()
        → tcp_input()
```

`nuttx/net/inet/inet_sockif.c`

### SYN listener lookup

`nuttx/net/tcp/tcp_input.c`

- Lines **710–724** locate the TCP header after the L2 and IPv4 headers.
- Lines **726–740** validate the TCP checksum.
- Lines **747–761** validate the TCP header offset/length.
- Lines **764–917** check active TCP connections.
- Lines **919–949** build the destination address/port and call `tcp_findlistener()`.
- Lines **951–964** verify that the packet is a SYN.
- Lines **966–969** require a free backlog container.
- Lines **981–1004** allocate the accepted TCP connection.
- Lines **1006–1019** silently drop the SYN if no TCP connection is available.
- Lines **1022–1031** construct the SYN-ACK.
- Lines **1034–1053** handle the no-listener case by sending a TCP RST.

This distinction is important:

- **No listener found**: normally produces a RST.
- **Listener found but backlog unavailable**: drops the SYN with no response.
- **Listener found but TCP connection allocation fails**: drops the SYN with no response.

The relevant diagnostic strings are:

- `tcp_input.c:1018`: `"ERROR: No free TCP connections"`
- `tcp_input.c:1034`: `"SYN with no listener (or old packet) .. reset"`

## 4. Why DHCP/ARP can work while TCP/80 produces no response

### A. The link type is unlikely to be the cause

ARP and TCP both pass through the same L2 path:

```text
BK RX full Ethernet frame
  → netdev_upper_rxpoll_work()
  → eth_input()
```

`eth_input()` identifies:

- ARP at lines **593–602**
- IPv4 at lines **569–578**

If ARP replies and DHCP replies are visible on the air, the following are already substantially proven:

- RX notification works.
- The lower-half `receive()` callback works.
- The frame starts with a valid Ethernet header.
- Bytes 12–13 contain usable EtherTypes.
- `NET_LL_IEEE80211` is reaching `eth_input()`.
- The driver’s TX path can send at least some generated Ethernet frames.

Changing only `NET_LL_IEEE80211` to `NET_LL_ETHERNET` would not change the `eth_input()` dispatch or the 14-byte header length in this tree.

### B. TCP checksum failure is possible

The `ai_agent` generated configuration has:

`cmake_out/bk7258-ap_ai_agent/.config`

- Line **1094**: `CONFIG_NET_IPV4_CHECKSUMS=y`
- Line **1133**: `CONFIG_NET_TCP_CHECKSUMS=y`
- Line **1134**: `CONFIG_NET_TCP_PREALLOC_CONNS=8`
- Line **1135**: `CONFIG_NET_TCP_ALLOC_CONNS=0`

The driver does not advertise RX checksum offload in the code examined. Therefore:

- IPv4 checksum is checked at `ipv4_input.c:473–485`.
- TCP checksum is checked at `tcp_input.c:726–740`.

DHCP can still work because the generated configuration has UDP checksum validation disabled:

`cmake_out/bk7258-ap_ai_agent/.config`

- Line **1165**: `# CONFIG_NET_UDP_CHECKSUMS is not set`

Therefore, “DHCP works” does not by itself prove that the TCP checksum arriving from the BK controller is valid.

A SYN that fails TCP checksum validation is dropped at `tcp_input.c:738–740` and produces no response.

### C. TCP backlog/connection resources can silently drop SYNs

`tcp_input.c:966–969` drops a SYN when no backlog container is available.

`nuttx/net/tcp/tcp_backlog.c`

- Lines **276–290**, `tcp_backlogavailable()`:
  - returns false when the listener has no free backlog container.
- Lines **215–255** show the backlog container allocation path and its `-ENOMEM` failure.

The source has an explicit application-level warning about this exact class of symptom:

`app/provisioning_web/vp_server.c`

- Lines **335–344**:

> “This requires `CONFIG_NET_TCPBACKLOG` on NuttX... Without it TCP_BACKLOG events never fire, POLLIN on a listening socket is unreachable, and accept() blocks with no timeout at all — measured on the board as a service that reported ‘listening’ and then answered nothing.”

### D. The build configurations differ

The `nsh` configuration does not enable TCP backlog:

`contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/boards/bk7258/bk7258-ap/configs/nsh/defconfig`

- Line **128**: `CONFIG_NET_TCP=y`
- There is no `CONFIG_NET_TCPBACKLOG=y` in this file.

The generated `nsh` configuration also shows backlog disabled:

`cmake_out/bk7258-ap_nsh/.config`

- Around line **1126**: TCP is enabled.
- Around line **1126** onward: `# CONFIG_NET_TCPBACKLOG is not set`.

By contrast, the `ai_agent` configuration enables it:

`board/beken/boards/bk7258/bk7258-ap/configs/ai_agent/defconfig`

- Line **159**: `CONFIG_NET_TCP=y`
- Line **160**: `CONFIG_NET_TCPBACKLOG=y`

Generated result:

`cmake_out/bk7258-ap_ai_agent/.config`

- Line **1153**: `CONFIG_NET_TCPBACKLOG=y`
- Line **1154**: `CONFIG_NET_TCPBACKLOG_CONNS=8`

Thus:

- If the failing image is the `nsh` image, missing TCP backlog is a confirmed configuration defect relevant to the documented HTTP failure.
- If the failing image is `ai_agent`, backlog is already enabled. Then the likely next checks are TCP checksum validation, listener startup, or exhaustion of the eight preallocated TCP connection structures.

### E. The HTTP server may not actually be running

The server is only created if `velasight_provisioning_start()` succeeds:

`vp_server.c:473–495`

A failed `socket()`, `bind()`, or `listen()` returns an error and no listener is registered.

For the VelaSight AP path, the expected startup sequence is:

- DHCP starts: `vs_network.c:243–250`
- HTTP listener starts: `vs_network.c:251–262`
- Server prints readiness: `vs_network.c:271–275`

If the SYN reaches the stack but there is no listener, NuttX should attempt an RST at `tcp_input.c:1034–1053`. If the client sees neither SYN-ACK nor RST, inspect the RX/TCP/TX stages rather than changing the link type.

## 5. TX path for a SYN-ACK/RST

After TCP creates a response:

`nuttx/net/tcp/tcp_send.c`

- `tcp_synack()` is lines **618–690**.
- It sets the packet length at lines **634–636**.
- It fills TCP options at lines **651–685**.
- `tcp_sendcommon()` builds checksums and records the outgoing packet; the IPv4 checksum/TCP checksum handling is around lines **230–245**.

For a reset:

- `tcp_reset()` is lines **392–554**.
- It swaps addresses/ports and sets RST/RST-ACK at lines **451–486**.
- It rebuilds the IPv4/TCP packet at lines **502–550**.

Then `devif_out()` builds the Ethernet/ARP part:

`nuttx/net/devif/devif_poll.c`

- Lines **1219–1253**
- Lines **1226–1238** explicitly handle both:

```c
case NET_LL_ETHERNET:
case NET_LL_IEEE80211:
    arp_out(dev);
```

Back in `eth_input()`:

`nuttx/drivers/net/netdev_upperhalf.c`

- Lines **612–624** queue any response with `dev->d_len > 0`.

The upper-half calls the lower-half transmit callback:

- `netdev_upper_txpoll()`: lines **284–327**
- Lower callback invocation: line **312**

BK7258 then:

`bk7258_wifi.c`

- Lines **1918–2005**, `wifi_transmit()`
- Copies the complete generated Ethernet frame at **1971**
- Queues it to the CP at **1994–1997**

Completion is handled as follows:

- `wifi_handle_data()` recognizes a completed TX slot at lines **1511–1529**
- It returns the retained netpkt at lines **1621–1629**
- `wifi_notify_network()` frees it and calls `netdev_lower_txdone()` at lines **1262–1265**
- `netdev_lower_txdone()` schedules further upper-half TX work at `netdev_upperhalf.c:1692–1708`

There is no indication in this path that `NET_LL_IEEE80211` suppresses or alters TCP responses.

## Minimal confirmed fix recommendation

### If the failing image is `bk7258-ap_nsh`

Enable TCP backlog in the board configuration:

```text
CONFIG_NET_TCPBACKLOG=y
```

The relevant file is:

```text
contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/
  board/beken/boards/bk7258/bk7258-ap/configs/nsh/defconfig
```

This is the minimal source-supported fix because:

1. The `nsh` configuration enables TCP but omits `CONFIG_NET_TCPBACKLOG`.
2. `vp_server.c:335–344` explicitly identifies missing backlog support as causing a server that reports listening but answers nothing.
3. The TCP input path has silent-drop cases when listener/backlog resources are unavailable.

### If the failing image is `bk7258-ap_ai_agent`

Do **not** change `NET_LL_IEEE80211` to `NET_LL_ETHERNET`; the AI-agent configuration already has:

```text
CONFIG_NET_TCPBACKLOG=y
```

at:

- `ai_agent/defconfig:160`
- generated `.config:1153`

For that image, the minimal recommendation is to instrument/observe these existing branches:

1. `bk7258_wifi.c:1577–1583` — confirm the incoming SYN is logged as `eth=0x0800`.
2. `ipv4_input.c:473–485` — check for bad IPv4 checksum.
3. `tcp_input.c:726–740` — check for bad TCP checksum.
4. `tcp_input.c:966–969` — check backlog availability.
5. `tcp_input.c:1006–1019` — check “No free TCP connections”.
6. `vp_server.c:473–495` — confirm port 80 `bind()` and `listen()` succeeded.
7. `bk7258_wifi.c:1983–1985` — confirm the generated SYN-ACK/RST is copied into a BK TX Ethernet frame.

**Bottom line:** the link-layer type is correct; the first concrete fix is enabling `CONFIG_NET_TCPBACKLOG` for the `nsh` build. For `ai_agent`, the failure is more likely TCP checksum validation, listener/resource exhaustion, or absence of the HTTP listener—not the `NET_LL_IEEE80211` registration.
